plan_a_advantages: Includes dedicated hill and threshold workouts for power and endurance.
Incorporates strength training to support trail-specific demands.
Offers a more varied training stimulus beyond just easy runs.
plan_b_advantages: Prioritizes recovery and freshness, which is essential for any training plan.
Features a longer, longer run to build aerobic base and time on feet.
Provides a more consistent, low-impact training schedule.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates a more targeted approach to building speed and strength specific to trail running. While Plan B prioritizes recovery and maintaining freshness, which is important, it lacks the structured intensity needed for significant improvement. Plan A includes dedicated hill workouts and threshold runs, crucial for developing the power and endurance required for faster trail times, alongside strength training to support these efforts. Plan B’s consistent easy runs, while beneficial for recovery, don’t provide the stimulus needed to actually increase speed.
